q1.q: What makes this different from a random prompt dump?
q1.a: The library is organized around actual use cases. You can filter by category, open a detailed page, and reuse a prompt with context instead of copying a vague one-liner.

q2.q: Can I use these prompts as templates for client work?
q2.a: Yes. The safest workflow is to treat them as starting structures, then replace placeholders with your audience, goal, constraints, and examples.

q3.q: How should I judge whether a prompt is good?
q3.a: A useful prompt should set a role, define the task clearly, add constraints, and describe the output format. We are gradually expanding detail pages around those criteria.

about.title: A prompt library built to be useful, not just large
about.intro: PentaPrompt is a curated AI prompt library focused on practical work scenarios. The goal is simple: help users start faster with prompts that are organized, searchable, and easier to adapt than scattered examples from social feeds or chat screenshots.

curated.title: Curated prompts
curated.desc: We group prompts by category and intent so users can find a workable starting point for a real task.

trust.title: Clear editorial structure
trust.desc: We are improving prompt pages with usage guidance, examples, and context so each page can stand on its own.

contact.title: Public contact
contact.desc: Users, partners, and reviewers can reach us through a visible site email instead of a hidden account.

howWeWork.title: How the library is organized
howWeWork.p1: The site is designed around common work categories such as writing, coding, marketing, SEO, learning, and video. That makes it easier to browse by intent and compare related prompts in one place.
howWeWork.p2: Each prompt page is meant to do more than show raw text. We are expanding pages with guidance on when to use a prompt, what input to provide, what output to expect, and what to watch out for before copying it into production work.
howWeWork.p3: We also maintain topic collections and a discovery page so search users can understand what the site covers before jumping into individual prompts.

q2.q: Which models are these prompts for?

q1.q: What are writing prompts used for?
q1.a: Use them to generate drafts faster, rewrite with a specific tone, and produce structured outputs like outlines and scripts.

q2.q: How do I avoid generic writing?
q2.a: Add your audience, angle, and constraints. Provide 2–3 examples of style, and ask for multiple variants.

q3.q: Do these work for long-form content?
q3.a: Yes. Start with an outline prompt, then expand section by section with clear constraints and sources.

q1.q: What do SEO prompts help with?
q1.a: They help you plan keyword clusters, create outlines, write meta descriptions, and produce content briefs aligned with search intent.

q2.q: Can AI-written content rank on Google?
q2.a: It can, if it is helpful and accurate. Use prompts to produce structured drafts, then add original insights and verification.

q3.q: How do I make outputs more actionable?
q3.a: Ask for tables, checklists, and step-by-step tasks. Specify target audience, funnel stage, and constraints.

q1.q: Which marketing assets can I generate?
q1.a: Ads, landing page copy, positioning statements, email sequences, and social posts.

q2.q: How do I keep messaging consistent?
q2.a: Provide your brand voice, product positioning, and a few examples. Ask for multiple variants and a final recommended option.

q3.q: What should I include as context?
q3.a: Your audience, offer, benefits, differentiators, objections, and any constraints like length or platform.

q1.q: Are coding prompts safe to use?
q1.a: They are a starting point. Always review code, run tests, and validate security and edge cases.

q2.q: How do I get better code outputs?
q2.a: Provide the stack, constraints, input/output examples, and ask for explanations plus tests.

q3.q: Can I use prompts for refactors?
q3.a: Yes. Ask for step-by-step refactor plans, risk assessment, and incremental changes with tests.

q1.a: They are templates for generating scripts, storyboards, shot lists, and structured instructions for video creation workflows.

q2.q: Which tools can I use them with?
q2.a: Most video prompts are tool-agnostic. You can adapt them for your preferred generator by mapping fields like style, camera, and length.

q3.q: How do I get more consistent results?
q3.a: Specify duration, structure, tone, and visual style. Ask for scene-by-scene outputs and a single global style guide.

editorial.title: How to use this prompt well
editorial.scenarioText: Use this prompt when you need {{category}} help and want a reusable structure instead of starting from scratch. It works especially well for tasks related to {{tags}}.
editorial.sampleInputText: Give the model the exact goal, target audience, constraints, and source context for {{title}}. Better inputs usually include examples, formatting rules, and any edge cases you already know about.
editorial.sampleOutputText: A strong result should return a usable draft, checklist, or structured answer aligned with {{category}} work. If the first output feels generic, add tighter constraints and ask for 2 to 3 variants.
editorial.note1: Replace placeholders with real context before copying this prompt into production work.
editorial.note2: If the output is too broad, add audience, tone, length, and formatting constraints.
editorial.note3: Review factual claims, links, and sensitive decisions before using the result publicly.
editorial.editorNoteText: This prompt is most valuable as a starting framework. The more specific your context is, the easier it becomes to turn the output into something genuinely useful.
